links.outcome: Reader diagnostic performance with vs without AI heatmap assistance, and overreliance assessment
links.effect: AI assistance (S2) improved accuracy 26.7%, sensitivity 41.0%, specificity 25.1%, F1 35.6%, precision 31.4% (all p<0.01); agreement with AI on AI-misclassified cases rose (S1 vs S2 p=0.037), suggesting automation bias.
links.quote: Significant improvements were observed during the S2 using AI heatmapping, with a 26.7% increase in accuracy, 25.1% in specificity, 41.0% in sensitivity, 35.6% in F1 score, and 31.4% in precision (all p-values < 0.01).

links.outcome: Whether users detect incorrect AI outputs / agreement with AI on AI-misclassified cases
links.effect: Median agreement with AI on misclassified CXRs was 50.0% in S1, 50.0% in S2, 50.0% in S3; significant differences S1 vs S2 (p=0.037) and S1 vs S3 (p=0.012), suggesting automation bias and carryover.
links.quote: Wilcoxon signed-rank tests with Bonferroni correction revealed significant differences between S1 and S2 ( p = 0.037) and between S1 and S3 ( p = 0.012).

links.outcome: Retention of diagnostic skill after AI withdrawal and overreliance concerns among trainees
links.effect: After AI withdrawal (S3) performance declined vs S2 but stayed above baseline for accuracy (+13.3%, p=0.010) and precision (+13.7%, p=0.010); 34.6% worried about over-reliance.
links.quote: However, slight improvements were still observed, with statistically significant improvements in accuracy (13.3%, p = 0.010) and precision (13.7%, p = 0.010).
